title: Surplus stipend & operator playbook for temporary surge handling
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a temporary surplus stipend mechanism (internal name: 'surge stipend') that grants short-lived headroom to Dedicated tenants during traffic spikes, coupled with clear operator runbooks and invoice treatment. This ticket covers the API flags, telemetry changes, billing reconciliation rules, autoscaler integration, and operator playbook for manual interventions. The goal is to provide predictable throughput for customers during surges while making billing transparent and minimizing charge surprises. The stipend should be limited by a per-tenant cap and decay window, support opt-out at contract level, and be auditable in logs and invoices.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by PM and Billing
Surge stipend control flags implemented in capacity service (on/off, max_units, decay_seconds)
Autoscaler consults stipend when calculating desired capacity (simulated in canary)
Billing pipeline emits stipend events tagged and visible in invoice preview UI
Operator playbook available in Confluence with run, rollback, and escalation steps
End-to-end canary exercise demonstrating a controlled spike with stipend used and no SLO regressions
steps: 1) Design and sequence: finalize stipend semantics and limits with PM and Billing
2) Add stipend flags to capacity allocator API and datastore (feature-flag gated)
3) Update autoscaler logic to include stipend headroom in desired_count and provide metrics
4) Emit stipend grant/expire events to billing event pipeline and add invoice sample rows
5) Create dashboards: stipend usage, per-tenant credits consumed, surge-incidents and SLO impact
6) Draft operator playbook and runbook; get oncall training session scheduled
7) Canary in staging with two tenants, run simulated spikes, validate metrics and invoices
8) Gradual rollout to 10% of tenants, monitor for 72h, then ramp to 100% behind contract opt-in
rollout_plan: Stage: internal-only for SRE and Billing team
Canary: 2 non-critical tenants in staging for 48h
Pilot: 10% in production (opt-in) for 72h with close SRE/Billing monitoring
Full: opt-in enabled for all Dedicated customers, auto-opt-out default for new contracts
Post-rollout: 30-day billing reconciliation audit and customer communication template
operator_playbook: When spike is ongoing and stipend exhausted: scale down load via rate-limiting rules and notify customer
If unexpected invoice entries occur: fetch stipend events (billing.event_id) and reconcile with request logs
To force-expire stipend for a tenant: POST /allocator/v1/tenants/{id}/stipend/expire with operator token
If autoscaler shows oscillation after stipend grant: toggle 'surge.stipend' flag to false for tenant and open incident
Escalation: page Billing Lead (pager: Nora Blake) for invoice disputes and Platform Lead (pager: Mateo Ruiz) for SLO regressions
billing_policy_summary: Stipend grants are free headroom up to X units per 24h window (configurable per contract)
Usage beyond stipend billed at regular dedicated rates with a separate 'post-stipend' invoice line
Stipend usage will be visible in invoice preview as 'Surge stipend adjustment' with timestamps
Stipend credits do not roll over; expired stipends are documented with event ids for audits
Operators can apply manual one-time credit adjustments for exceptional cases via Billing tools
open_questions: What should the default per-tenant stipend cap be for existing contracts?
Should stipend be applied per-cluster or global tenant-wide when tenants span multiple pools?
Do we expose stipend consumption to customers in realtime via Console or only in invoice previews?
How to avoid stipend gaming (rapid on/off traffic to repeatedly consume small stipends)?
What SLA guarantees (if any) do we give when serving via stipend headroom?
